title: JavaScript Event Loop Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict event-loop execution order and identify microtask, macrotask, rendering, and long-task behavior.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: The timer callback is scheduled as a later task. Synchronous logs run first.
The promise callback is a microtask, so it runs after synchronous code finishes.
Synchronous logs run first, then the promise microtask, then the timer task.
Microtasks drain fully before the timer task runs. The second promise callback is queued as another microtask.
After each task, microtasks run before the next task. The promise created in Timer 1 runs before Timer 2.

options.text: The long synchronous loop blocks the main thread
Click handlers always run in parallel
The browser renders between every loop iteration

questions.explanation: Long synchronous work keeps the call stack busy, delaying rendering and input handling.

options.text: It can starve timers and rendering by endlessly scheduling microtasks

questions.explanation: The microtask queue drains before tasks/rendering. Endless microtasks can prevent the loop from moving on.
Even already-resolved promises schedule `.then()` callbacks as microtasks.

options.text: The long task can block rendering until after both DOM changes
DOM updates are not allowed in JavaScript

questions.explanation: The browser may not paint while JavaScript is blocking the main thread.

questions.prompt: What is a good use for `requestAnimationFrame`?

options.text: Scheduling visual updates before the next repaint
Parsing JSON on a background thread automatically

questions.explanation: `requestAnimationFrame` is designed for animation and visual updates aligned with rendering.

questions.prompt: If a timer is set for 100ms but the call stack is busy for 2 seconds, when can the timer callback run?

options.text: Only after the stack becomes clear
Never, because timers are cancelled by loops

questions.explanation: Timer delays are minimum delays. The callback cannot run while the call stack is busy.

questions.prompt: What is the best first step when predicting event-loop output?

options.text: Identify and run all synchronous code first

questions.explanation: Synchronous stack code runs before queued microtasks and tasks.

options.text: Async callbacks still run on the call stack when executed
Async callbacks never use the call stack

questions.explanation: Async callbacks are scheduled for later, but when they execute, they still run on the JavaScript call stack.

questions.prompt: What can help with heavy CPU work that should not freeze the browser UI?
questions.explanation: Web Workers can run CPU-heavy work off the main thread.

questions.prompt: Which ordering model is most useful for beginner event-loop prediction?

options.text: Synchronous stack code, then microtasks, then tasks
Tasks, then microtasks, then synchronous code

questions.explanation: The simplified model stack -> microtasks -> tasks predicts many common examples.
